hints: Interpret each complex condition geometrically before finding their intersection.
Draw the closed disc of radius $1$ centred at $-1+i$, including its circular boundary.
From the point $1$ on the real axis, draw the ray with argument $3\pi/4$ and determine the side satisfying the argument inequality.
Shade only the overlap, with solid boundaries because equality is allowed.
walkthrough:
Interpret the first condition $|z + 1 - \mathrm{i}| \le 1$ in the Argand diagram:
Rewrite as $|z - (-1 + \mathrm{i})| \le 1$. This represents the set of all points inside and on the boundary of a solid circle with centre $(-1, 1)$ and radius $1$.

Determine the key points of the circle $|z - (-1 + \mathrm{i})| = 1$:
- The circle touches the real axis at $(-1, 0)$ because the distance from the centre $(-1, 1)$ to the real axis is $1$.
- The circle touches the imaginary axis at $(0, 1)$ because the distance from the centre $(-1, 1)$ to the imaginary axis is $1$.

Interpret the second condition $\arg(z - 1) \le \dfrac{3}{4}\pi$:
This condition defines a half-plane bounded by a ray emanating from the fixed point $z = 1$ (coordinates $(1, 0)$) at an angle of $\dfrac{3}{4}\pi = 135^\circ$ to the positive real axis.

Verify the boundary ray passing from $(1, 0)$:
The ray has gradient $\tan(135^\circ) = -1$ and equation $y - 0 = -1(x - 1) \implies y = -x + 1$.
At $x = 0$, $y = 1$, so this boundary ray passes exactly through the point $(0, 1)$ on the imaginary axis where the circle touches it.

Shade the region:
Shade the interior and boundary of the circle that lies on or below the half-line $\arg(z - 1) = \dfrac{3}{4}\pi$ starting from $(1, 0)$.

ai_rubric.Argand Loci: Displays a circle with centre $-1+i$. Displays a circle of radius 1 with centre not at the origin, or the relevant part. The intersection of the closed unit disc centred at $-1+i$ with the half-plane on the side of the ray from $1$ at argument $3\pi/4$.
